message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights | What It Means for You | |------|------------|-----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | Keep a copy of the lease, move‑in inspection report, and receipts for any repairs you paid for. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must comply with all local building, health, and safety codes. | If something is broken, give written notice and allow reasonable time for repair. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix a major issue within a reasonable time, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent (up to the amount of the security deposit). | Document the problem, send a written notice, and keep receipts. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Rent Increase**: Must give at least **30 days’ written notice** for a rent increase.
• **Eviction**: Must give at least **30 days’ written notice** for nonpayment of rent; otherwise, you can file a lawsuit to stop eviction. | Keep copies of all notices. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) unless it’s an emergency. | If the landlord enters without notice, you can ask them to leave and document the incident. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income (including public assistance). | If you suspect discrimination, you can file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, you can break the lease only if the landlord breaches the lease or if you have a “just cause” (e.g., domestic violence). | Provide written notice and keep proof of delivery. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease. Late fees are allowed but must be reasonable and disclosed in the lease. | Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if needed. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect your privacy and cannot conduct searches without a warrant or court order, except in emergencies. | If you feel your privacy is violated, consult an attorney. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If the landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the Texas Commission on Human Rights, or file a civil action in court. | Keep all documentation (emails, texts, photos, receipts). | #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Read the Lease Thoroughly** – Look for clauses about security deposits, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document the Condition** – Take photos or videos of the unit before you move in. 3. **Ask About Repairs** – Clarify who pays for what (e.g., HVAC, plumbing). 4. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities have additional tenant protections. #### When Things Go Wrong - **Nonpayment of Rent**: Give a 30‑day written notice. If the landlord still tries to evict, you can file a **“Stop Eviction”** lawsuit in the county court. - **Unlawful Entry**: Document the entry and notify the landlord in writing that you consider it unlawful. - **Maintenance Issues**: Send a written notice, keep copies, and give the landlord a reasonable time to fix. If they don’t, you may repair and deduct or pursue a claim for damages. #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights**: [https://www.tchra.org](https://www.tchra.org) - **Local Housing Authorities**: Many counties have tenant‑rights hotlines. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you’re entitled to a safe, habitable home, timely notice for rent changes or eviction, protection against discrimination, and the right to repair and deduct if the landlord fails to maintain the property. Keep thorough records, communicate in writing, and know where to seek help if your rights are violated.
